heuristics.rule: Secure offer letter and confirm start date before resigning
heuristics.condition: When changing jobs during OPT period...
heuristics.action: Do not resign until you have a signed offer letter with a confirmed start date, ensuring the gap between jobs stays well under 90 days cumulative
heuristics.because: The 90-day unemployment limit is cumulative across the entire OPT period, not per job change. A gap that feels manageable can push you over the limit when combined with earlier gaps.

heuristics.rule: Notify DSO and update SEVIS within 10 days of starting new job
heuristics.condition: When any job change occurs during OPT...
heuristics.action: Contact your DSO on the day you resign or start the new job to initiate SEVIS record update — do not wait
heuristics.because: SEVIS update is a regulatory requirement tied to F-1 status maintenance; the poster confirmed this is DSO-operated, not self-service, and delay risks status violation

heuristics.rule: For STEM OPT job changes, ensure E-Verify registration and I-983 are completed before first day of work
heuristics.condition: When switching employers on STEM OPT...
heuristics.action: Confirm new employer's E-Verify registration status and submit I-983 Training Plan before the start date, not after onboarding
heuristics.because: The poster explicitly states these must be completed before work begins, not retroactively — retroactive filing creates a compliance gap in STEM OPT authorization

decision_factors.factor: Cumulative unemployment days used so far during OPT
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The 90-day limit is cumulative across the entire OPT period, so prior gaps from earlier job searches or between graduation and first job all count toward the same clock
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review your SEVIS record and employment history timeline to count all days not formally employed in an OPT-qualifying role since OPT start date

decision_factors.factor: New employer's E-Verify registration status (for STEM OPT)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: STEM OPT work authorization requires the employer to be enrolled in E-Verify before employment begins; working without this voids STEM OPT authorization
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask HR directly to confirm E-Verify participation and request the E-Verify Company ID number before accepting the offer

decision_factors.factor: Whether freelance or 1099 work counts toward OPT employment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Ambiguity about whether freelance work qualifies as OPT employment affects how many unemployment days are actually accumulating — a common gray area raised in comments
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Consult DSO directly; self-employment and freelance eligibility under OPT is school/DSO-dependent and field-of-study dependent

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Resigning before securing a new job offer to 'take time to find the right fit'
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Each day unemployed counts toward the 90-day cumulative cap across the entire OPT period — a gap that seems acceptable in isolation can become a status violation when combined with earlier gaps
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who had any gap between graduation and first job, or who took time off between prior roles, and assume their remaining unemployment budget resets

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Assuming OPT EAD card tied to original employer is invalid after job change
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Students may unnecessarily panic or apply for new EAD when the existing EAD remains valid — the card does not list a specific employer as a restriction
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: First-time job changers on OPT who conflate the EAD document with employer-specific authorization

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Delaying I-983 submission until after STEM OPT onboarding paperwork
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Working even one day without a completed I-983 and confirmed E-Verify registration may constitute unauthorized employment under STEM OPT rules
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students whose new employers are unfamiliar with STEM OPT compliance requirements and treat I-983 as routine HR paperwork rather than a pre-employment requirement

failure_patterns.pattern: Resigning first, then job searching — resulting in unemployment gap exceeding 90 days
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students treat OPT like regular employment and apply standard job-search logic ('quit, then look seriously') without accounting for the cumulative unemployment cap
failure_patterns.consequence: The original poster gapped 95 days, exceeding the 90-day limit; comment [1] corroborates this pattern with an H-1B RFE triggered by a 4-month gap
warning_signs: Student says 'I want to take a break before my next job'
Student does not know how many unemployment days they have already used
Student treats the 90-day limit as per-episode rather than cumulative

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming the 90-day unemployment limit resets or is per-job-change rather than cumulative
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The word 'limit' implies a single threshold that either has or hasn't been crossed, not a running counter that accumulates across the entire OPT period
failure_patterns.consequence: Students believe they have more runway than they do; comment [1] describes an H-1B RFE being triggered by this exact misunderstanding
warning_signs: Student asks 'how long can I take off between jobs?' without mentioning prior gaps
Student references '90 days per gap' rather than '90 days total'

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating STEM OPT compliance documents (I-983, E-Verify) as post-hire paperwork
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Standard US onboarding (I-9, W-4, direct deposit) happens after the start date, so students and even HR teams assume all employment paperwork follows the same timeline
failure_patterns.consequence: Working before I-983 and E-Verify are in place may constitute unauthorized employment, potentially jeopardizing STEM OPT validity and future H-1B eligibility
warning_signs: Employer says 'we'll handle that after you start'
Student asks if I-983 can be submitted after the start date (comment [3])

diagnostic_questions.question: How many total days have you already been unemployed since your OPT start date — including the gap before your first job?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student actually has runway left in their 90-day cumulative budget, or is already close to or over the limit
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If they've already used 60+ days: any job change gap must be kept under 30 days — offer-in-hand before resignation is mandatory
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If they have a clean record with few gap days: they have more flexibility but should still not resign without an offer

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you confirmed your new employer is enrolled in E-Verify before accepting the STEM OPT role?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the STEM OPT employment will be legally valid from day one
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Request their E-Verify Company ID and confirm I-983 will be signed before your start date
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do not begin work until E-Verify registration is confirmed — working without it may void STEM OPT authorization

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your freelance or contract work qualify as OPT-authorized employment under your school's DSO guidelines?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether days doing freelance work are counting as employed or unemployed toward the 90-day cap
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Ensure you have documentation (contracts, field-of-study relevance justification) in case of future RFE
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Those days are accruing toward the 90-day unemployment limit — factor them into your gap calculation

industry_realities.common_belief: The 90-day unemployment limit on OPT is per job gap, so each job change gives you a fresh 90-day window
industry_realities.actual_reality: The 90-day limit is cumulative across the entire OPT period — all unemployment days from OPT start date to OPT end date are added together
industry_realities.implication: Students must track their total unemployment days from OPT start, not just their current gap — even a prior 30-day gap before their first job reduces future flexibility

industry_realities.common_belief: When you change jobs on OPT, you need a new EAD card because the card is tied to your employer
industry_realities.actual_reality: The OPT EAD card is not employer-specific and does not need to be reissued when changing jobs — the card itself remains valid
industry_realities.implication: Students can accept a new job without waiting for a new EAD, eliminating a false administrative bottleneck in the job change process

industry_realities.common_belief: SEVIS updates during OPT job changes are something the student handles directly
industry_realities.actual_reality: SEVIS updates are made by the DSO (Designated School Official), not the student — the student must notify the DSO who then performs the update
industry_realities.implication: Students must proactively contact their DSO immediately upon job change; the update does not happen automatically and cannot be self-filed

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Treats the 90-day rule as a per-gap limit and assumes each new job search gives a fresh 90-day window; does not track running total
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Maintains a personal log of all unemployment days from OPT start date; calculates remaining days before deciding how long a job search can safely take
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Exceeding 90 days cumulative can trigger H-1B RFEs, create status violations, and jeopardize future immigration filings — as seen in both the post and comment [1]

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Resigns first to 'focus on the job search,' then begins applying
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Obtains offer letter with confirmed start date before resigning, leaving only a minimal pre-planned buffer between jobs
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The naive approach risks status violation; the informed approach keeps the gap predictable and within legal limits

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes I-983 and E-Verify are onboarding paperwork to be handled after the start date, like other HR forms
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Treats I-983 and E-Verify confirmation as pre-conditions for employment — raises these with HR during offer negotiation, not after accepting
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Working even briefly without compliant STEM OPT documentation may constitute unauthorized employment with serious status consequences

community_misconceptions.misconception: The 90-day unemployment rule on OPT resets with each job change — it's 90 days per gap, not total
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The rule is usually taught in the context of a single job search, and '90 days' sounds like a per-episode allowance rather than a lifetime budget on OPT
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: The 90-day limit is cumulative across the entire OPT authorization period — all days not employed in a qualifying role since OPT start date count toward one shared total
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: A student who had a 60-day gap before their first job believes they have 90 days available for a new job search, but actually only has 30 days left — exceeding this triggers status violations and can surface in H-1B RFEs as seen in comment [1]

community_misconceptions.misconception: You need to apply for a new OPT EAD card when you change employers
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The EAD card is associated with OPT and students assume it functions like an employer-sponsored visa document that must be reissued per employer
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: OPT EAD cards are not employer-specific; the card remains valid for the duration of the OPT period regardless of employer changes
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Students may delay accepting new jobs, create unnecessary administrative burdens, or incorrectly believe they cannot work legally until a new card arrives — wasting unemployment days toward the 90-day cap

community_misconceptions.misconception: I-983 for STEM OPT can be submitted after the start date as part of normal onboarding
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Most US employment paperwork (I-9, W-4) is completed on or after the first day of work, so students and HR alike assume I-983 follows the same timeline
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: I-983 Training Plan and E-Verify enrollment must be in place before the student begins work under STEM OPT — not retroactively
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Working before I-983 and E-Verify are completed may constitute unauthorized employment, creating a compliance gap that could affect STEM OPT validity and future H-1B petitions

real_case_outcomes.situation: Student on OPT resigned before securing a new job, intending to job search while unemployed
real_case_outcomes.decision: Resigned first, then searched — resulting in a 95-day unemployment gap
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Exceeded the 90-day cumulative unemployment limit; DSO intervened to attempt remediation, but the student experienced significant anxiety and status risk
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Always secure an offer with a confirmed start date before resigning; the 90-day cap is cumulative and does not reset — even a few extra days of searching can push you over

real_case_outcomes.situation: Student on OPT (implied from comment [1]) had a 4-month unemployment gap during their OPT period, believing it was permissible
real_case_outcomes.decision: Did not monitor cumulative unemployment days and allowed a 4-month gap
real_case_outcomes.outcome: H-1B petition received an RFE specifically questioning the 4-month unemployment period during OPT
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Unemployment violations during OPT do not disappear — they resurface during H-1B adjudication as RFEs, potentially jeopardizing the H-1B petition years later

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student asks 'I already resigned, how do I fix this?' or 'I've been unemployed for X days, am I okay?'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Catastrophizing combined with decision paralysis — the student knows something may be wrong but is frozen by fear of confirming the violation
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Delays contacting DSO, searches online forums for reassurance rather than acting, hopes the gap won't be noticed
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe urgency: contacting DSO immediately gives the most options for remediation; delay only reduces options. The DSO has seen this before and can help — but only if contacted promptly

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student on OPT considering quitting a difficult job 'to take a real break and reset before the next search'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Burnout and present-bias — the psychological cost of current suffering outweighs the abstract future risk of status violation
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Student rationalizes that 90 days is 'plenty of time' to find a new job, ignoring cumulative days already used and job search variability
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Make the abstract concrete: calculate exactly how many unemployment days remain in the budget. If the number is under 45, a casual 'break-then-search' strategy is statistically high-risk given typical job search timelines

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student asks whether freelance work 'counts' while clearly hoping the answer is yes to reduce their unemployment day count
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Motivated reasoning — student wants confirmation that their current situation is compliant, not an accurate assessment of risk
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Posts the question framed as a clarification request, but is actually seeking reassurance; may act on forum answers rather than consulting DSO
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Redirect to authoritative source: 'This is exactly the question to bring to your DSO with documentation of the freelance work — forum answers on this are unreliable because it depends on your school's interpretation and your field of study'

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I change jobs on OPT without problems?
reframing_moves.reframe: The question isn't about the job change itself — OPT is your authorization, not your employer's. The question is how many unemployment days you have left and whether your new employer meets STEM OPT requirements before day one.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts focus from process compliance (paperwork) to status arithmetic (cumulative days) and pre-employment verification — the two variables that actually determine risk
reframing_moves.example_language: OPT是你的工作许可，不是雇主的担保 ('OPT is your work authorization, not your employer's guarantee')

reframing_moves.original_framing: I've been unemployed for a while on OPT — am I okay?
reframing_moves.reframe: The answer depends entirely on how many days you've been unemployed since your OPT start date in total — not just in this current gap. What's your running count?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Forces the student to calculate a concrete number rather than seeking reassurance, converting anxiety into actionable arithmetic
reframing_moves.example_language: 90天是累计计算的（不是单次）— 'the 90 days is cumulative, not per episode'
